analysis.description: The paper describes Perceptual Generative Autoencoders (PGAs), a novel framework for training autoencoder-based generative models. PGAs are designed to map target distributions to a latent space using an encoder and train the decoder to match the target distribution in this latent space. This approach addresses the challenge of intrinsic dimension discrepancies in data and ambient space. The paper demonstrates PGAs can be combined with variational autoencoders (VAEs) to improve sample quality and achieve state-of-the-art performance on datasets like CIFAR-10 and CelebA.
